summary: Iteration 47: frontend-only test of the German Commentary Collection. Web preview at 390x844 and 360x640. Every browser run blocked /api/**: 0 API calls and 0 pageerrors. The Node suite passed 42/42 and tsc --noEmit is clean. PASS: Joh 1,1 shows Streitenberger and Calvin. Ps 1,1 shows Kroeker and Rieger. 1Mo 1,1 shows Ansorg and Kroeker. Röm 8,28 shows Streitenberger, Calvin and Rieger. The panel never shows Matthew Henry or English text; MHCC appears only as a link in 'Weitere Quellen'. Each card shows author – title, range, 'Sprache: Deutsch', edition, year, Tradition and Rechte. No HTML/OSIS tags and no '\par' in the text. Tradition chips toggle every source of a tradition, and turning all traditions off shows commentary-empty. Preferences persist after reload: 'Reformiert only' stays after reload. Compare toggles to a side-by-side row. /study/sources shows the 5 sources as 'Eingebunden', MHCC and Bengel as 'Rechte nicht bestätigt – nicht eingebunden', and JW, Sefaria and bibelkommentare.de as 'Nur externer Link'. Performance: 1Mo 1,1 commentary renders in about 0.1s and expanding the 36k-char Kroeker text takes about 0.05s, with no freeze. Regression: reader chapter navigation, the xref tab (preview → 'Im Zusammenhang lesen' → return banner), the station flow (tora-1-1 phases 1→3), the world page and the library all work. FAIL/ISSUES: (1) BUG: turning off the last visible source with the source chips brings ALL sources back instead of showing the empty state. (2) The data marks 1,611 range entries (Kroeker 943, Rieger 668, Streitenberger 2) as scope 'verse', so the UI labels them '(Einzelvers)', e.g. 'Römer 8,28–39 (Einzelvers)'. (3) Ansorg verse mapping: 475/705 sermons carry a 'Stelle: X a:b-c' range but are mapped to their first verse only. (4) Kroeker OCR quality: 1,027/1,085 entries contain OCR artifacts. (5) On mobile the compare view is unreadable, and the 10 filter chips push the first card below the fold. (6) The web dev bundle is now 43.7 MB because the 25 MB commentary JSON is inlined.

ui_bugs.issue: Turning off the last remaining visible source via source-filter-<id> sets prefSources to [], which means 'all'. All 5 sources reappear and every chip turns back on, instead of showing commentary-empty. Reproduce: Röm 8,28, all on, then tap off calvin-de, kroeker, rieger, ansorg, streitenberger in turn. The last tap restores all 3 cards. RCA: VerseStudy.tsx:80. The `on ? commSources.filter(...)` branch never maps an empty result to ['none']; the tradition handler does this at line 70.

Range entries are labelled '(Einzelvers)', and the hint '– keine Einzelerklärung zu V. x' is suppressed. Examples: 'Römer 8,28–39 (Einzelvers)' for Rieger, and Ps 1,1–6 for Kroeker and Rieger. RCA: backend/scripts/import_sword_commentaries.py:52 extends 'to' for linked verses but keeps scope='verse'. 1,611 entries are affected.

When the user's filters hide everything, commentary-empty still says 'Für diesen Vers ist noch kein zulässig eingebundener Studienkommentar vorhanden'. That is misleading. It should say that sources are hidden by the filters and offer a 'show all' action.

integration_issues.issue: 475/705 Ansorg entries have a 'Stelle: <Buch> c:a-b' header that differs from their mapping, which covers only from=to=a. Example: ansorg-1-1-1 covers 1. Mose 1:1-31, yet it appears only on 1Mo 1,1 and not on 1Mo 1,2–31. Same for Neh 1:1-11 and Mt 4:3-19. Fix: parse 'Stelle:' in the importer and set to/scope='range' (and handle ranges that cross chapters).

1,027/1,085 Kroeker entries contain OCR artifacts. Examples: hyphenation splits like 'heid- nischen' and 'Verständ- nis'; 'ı8ff.' and '7f£.'; 'Hebr. 1, if.' instead of 1,1f.; and an HTML entity in 'Heilsverhei> Bungen' (kroeker-19-87-1). Smaller counts of hyphen splits appear in Streitenberger (93), Calvin (63), Ansorg (13) and Rieger (6). Consider a de-hyphenation pass ('([a-zäöüß])- ([a-zäöüß])' → '$1$2'), html.unescape, and a 'OCR-Text' note on Kroeker cards.

issues: Compare puts all hits in one flex row. With 3 cards at 360px, each column is about 95px wide and words break mid-word ('Streitenb erger', 'Kommen tar'). The badge is clipped. Use horizontal paging with about 85% card width, or limit to 2 columns.

5 tradition chips plus 5 author chips plus compare take 5 rows. At 360x640 the first card starts at y≈765, below the fold; at 390x844 it starts at y≈645. Collapse the filters into a 'Filter (5/5)' disclosure or a horizontal scroller.
The filter chips are 36px tall, under the 44px touch-target minimum (styles.chip minHeight:36). The 'Quelle (externer Link)' rows are also 36px.
The edition line exposes technical module names ('SWORD-Modul deuStreitenbergerKommentar (GermanSwordModules)'). Acceptable, but noisy on mobile.

action_items: HIGH: VerseStudy.tsx:80. In the source-chip handler, compute next and set prefSources to next.length ? next : ['none'], so that switching off the last source shows the empty state instead of 'all'. Also strip 'none' when re-adding a source.
MEDIUM: import_sword_commentaries.py:52. When linked verses extend an entry, set scope='range' and regenerate the commentary JSON. 1,611 entries are labelled 'Einzelvers' wrongly.
MEDIUM: Ansorg (MAK) importer. Derive from/to from the 'Stelle:' header (475 entries) so that sermons appear on every verse they cover.
MEDIUM: Clean the text. Join hyphenation splits, html.unescape (kroeker-19-87-1 '>'), and optionally fix common OCR glyphs (ı→1, £→f) for Kroeker, or label Kroeker as OCR text.
MEDIUM: Rework the mobile compare layout (horizontal scroll or 2 columns) and collapse the filter chips. Raise chip minHeight to 44.
LOW: Make the empty-state wording distinguish 'filtered out' from 'no commentary', and add a 'Alle Quellen anzeigen' button.

LOW/PERF: The dev web bundle is 43.7 MB, with a 20.9s first load in preview, because the 25 MB commentary JSON is inlined by Metro. Lazy require() does not split the bundle. Consider shipping the commentaries as assets (expo-asset/expo-file-system) or a SQLite DB to cut bundle size and memory on native.

LOW: The MHCC status says 'Rechte nicht bestätigt', but its license text says gemeinfrei and that it is hidden only because it is English. A dedicated status such as 'Ausgeblendet (nur englisch)' would be more accurate. Its English title still appears as a link under 'Weitere Quellen'.
critical_code_review_comments: VerseStudy.tsx:63-68: the tradition handler uses `active = pref.length ? pref : all`. When pref contains 'none', 'none' is carried into next, so next.length never equals all.length and the store keeps ['none', ...all] instead of resetting to []. This works, but the state is not normalised.
VerseStudy.tsx:23: the commentary filter runs permittedOffline(find) for every entry. That is O(n·sources), which is fine at the current size; precomputing an id Set would be cleaner.
The importer resets `prev` per chapter, so linked sections that cross a chapter boundary are split. Acceptable, but undocumented.

success_rate.frontend: 85% – all requested flows work; 1 filter bug, 2 data-mapping issues, OCR quality and mobile layout issues

seed_data_creation: None. Only browser localStorage in fresh Playwright contexts was used.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Close the intro: intro-skip-button, then welcome-start. Open the verse sheet: goto /bible?b=<Code>&ch=<c>&v=<v>, wait for verse-<c>-<v>, wait 1.5s, then do a normal click (a force click right after load does NOT open the sheet). Wait 0.7s, then click verse-tab-comm. The cards are found via [data-testid^=commentary-scope-]. A chip is active when its backgroundColor is rgb(47, 95, 122). Run python3 /app/tests/commentary_data_check.py for data checks (mapping, scope, OCR, Ansorg Stelle). Working routes: /station/tora-1-1 and /world/tora.
rca_of_issue: Source-chip bug: prefSources=[] is overloaded to mean 'all sources'. When the source-chip off-branch filters out the last id, it returns [], not ['none']. Scope bug: the importer extends e.to for linked SWORD verses without updating e.scope. Ansorg mapping: the MAK module stores each sermon at its first verse only; the real range is only in the 'Stelle:' text header.
